title: Directional assimilation in accelerator anomaly classifiers: the ACRB hypotheses
description: The Accelerator Classifier Retention Battery sets out six standing hypotheses on directional assimilation in real-time learned selection: reconstruction-specific failure, cross-family persistence, the normalized-autoencoder remedy, the low-complexity blind spot, blind-spot inheritance through distillation, and drift under quantization and firmware. Inversion Battery v0.2 reports that only 36 to 47 percent of a teacher's top one percent survives into the student's, with the loss in distillation, and lists what is deferred to v0.3. The common experiment proposed is to calibrate each model at matched operating points and measure how much of a withheld class is assimilated as ordinary.

claims.registered_title: Assimilation Across Accelerator Classifier Architectures: A Cross-Family Metrology of Directional Failure in Real-Time Learned Selection (EA-SEI-ACRB-01 v1.0)
claims.statement: The Accelerator Classifier Retention Battery proposes a common experiment: reverse the normal/anomalous direction where meaningful; calibrate each model at matched own-background operating points; measure the fraction of a withheld class that is assimilated as ordinary; repeat across representations and architectures; follow the score through quantization, distillation, and firmware transformation; and measure whether different models miss the same events.

claims.registered_title: Inversion Battery v0.2: Multi-Seed Direction-Dependence, a Correction Ledger, and Four Rejected Overclaims (EA-SEI-BATTERY-01 v2.0)
claims.statement:
## 8. What is deferred to v0.3

A faithful normalized-autoencoder and Wasserstein variant port; a pooled complexity axis with common standardization and quantization, and a distance-matched panel, before any hypothesis test on complexity; hierarchical uncertainty over events as well as seeds, with a larger calibration split so the severe operating point is not set by roughly twenty tail events; the full miss-overlap measurement across seeds and operating points; and a GPU pass at scale.

claims.registered_title: Inversion Battery v0.2: Multi-Seed Direction-Dependence, a Correction Ledger, and Four Rejected Overclaims (EA-SEI-BATTERY-01 v2.0)
claims.statement: The failure is not universally oriented. The encoder-side latent score alone escapes the T1 inversion (0.535 / 0.739) while carrying the largest T1 asymmetry. Architecture changes the orientation of the blind spot — which is the strongest available argument for a cross-family battery rather than a single-model critique.

statements.quote: The failure is not universally oriented. The encoder-side latent score alone escapes the T1 inversion (0.535 / 0.739) while carrying the largest T1 asymmetry. Architecture changes the orientation of the blind spot — which is the strongest available argument for a cross-family battery rather than a single-model critique.

> **With model weights fixed, changing the score function is sufficient to reverse the directional ordering of the anomaly relation.**

This falsifies architecture *alone* as the explanation. It does not show that architecture and training can never affect orientation.
statements.falsifier: The score-ablation result fails if reading multiple scores off fixed weights at matched operating points shows consistent orientation across readouts on other pairs.

states.change: reversed: v0.3 falsifies the v0.2 attribution to architecture; with weights fixed, changing the score function suffices to reverse the ordering (architecture and readout were confounded in v0.2)
